summary: Game crashes when replacing a block with a wall with blockstate up:false
description: Give yourself a wall using give @p brick_wall{BlockStateTag:{up:"false"}} 1 Then, place a block with no other blocks around it, and press left and right click at the same time while looking at that block and holding the wall. Then, crash.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft.
2. Enter Creative mode using the command `/gamemode creative`.
3. Give yourself a brick wall with the specific blockstate using the command `give @p brick_wall{BlockStateTag:{up:"false"}} 1`.
4. Place any block on the ground with no other blocks around it.
5. Hold the brick wall in your hand.
6. Look at the placed block and press left and right click simultaneously while holding the brick wall.
7. Observe that the game crashes.
Observed Behavior: When attempting to replace a block with a brick wall that has the blockstate `up:false`, the game crashes under specific conditions. To reproduce this issue, first give yourself a brick wall item using the command `/give @p brick_wall{BlockStateTag:{up:"false"}} 1`. Next, place a single block in an open area without any adjacent blocks. While holding the brick wall item and looking at the placed block, simultaneously press left and right click. This action triggers a game crash. The crash occurs specifically when attempting to replace the block with the brick wall that has its `up` property set to false. This detailed sequence of steps is crucial for developers to replicate and address the issue effectively.
Expected Behavior: When following the steps provided, the game should not crash. Instead, placing a brick wall with blockstate `up:false` next to an isolated block and pressing left and right click simultaneously should simply result in the brick wall being placed or replaced without any adverse effects on the game's stability. The player should be able to continue playing normally.
